record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Does an apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution, or can one give an explicit counterexample; under what spacetime conditions can a trapped surface be extended indefinitely to a spacelike 3-cylinder of trapped surfaces with non-increasing area?

evidence.quote: Does an apparent horizon persist under the Einstein evolution? This is probably false, but I don't know of an explicit counterexample. An argument giving spacetime conditions under which a trapped surface can be indefinitely extended to a spacelike 3-cylinder of trapped surfaces, of non-increasing area, is given in [IW2].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth globally hyperbolic spacetime satisfying the Einstein field equations, and let $\Sigma_0 \subset M$ be a smooth Cauchy hypersurface containing an apparent horizon $H_0$ (the outermost marginally outer trapped surface in $\Sigma_0$, i.e., a smooth closed 2-surface on which the expansion $\theta_+$ of outgoing future-directed null geodesics vanishes, bounding a region in which $\theta_+ \le 0$). Consider a smooth foliation $\{\Sigma_t\}_{t \ge 0}$ of a neighborhood of $\Sigma_0$ in the future by Cauchy hypersurfaces.

(a) Must the apparent horizon persist under Einstein evolution? That is, does each later slice $\Sigma_t$ necessarily contain an apparent horizon $H_t$, with the family $\{H_t\}$ forming a (piecewise) smooth tube in $M$? Either prove persistence under suitable hypotheses, or exhibit an explicit spacetime counterexample in which the apparent horizon disappears under evolution.

(b) Identify spacetime conditions (for instance on the matter model, energy conditions, or the geometry near $H_0$) under which a given (marginally) trapped 2-surface in $\Sigma_0$ can be extended indefinitely to the future as a spacelike 3-dimensional cylinder of trapped 2-surfaces whose areas are monotonically non-increasing.
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive counterexample to apparent-horizon persistence under Einstein evolution appears in the literature, and the question of generic persistence remains unresolved. Partial results exist establishing existence and smoothness of marginally outer trapped tubes / dynamical horizons under specific stability or energy assumptions (work of Andersson–Mars–Simon, Ashtekar–Krishnan, etc.), and conditional extension theorems to spacelike 3-cylinders of trapped surfaces with non-increasing area are known, but the general problem stays open.

status_evidence.title: Apparent horizon - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Apparent horizons are not invariant properties of spacetime, and in particular, they are distinct from event horizons.
status_evidence.claim: Apparent horizons depend on the slicing, so their evolution under Einstein equations is nontrivial and not automatically guaranteed.

status_evidence.title: The Area of Horizons and the Trapped Region
status_evidence.snippet: Sequence of MOTS forming a marginally outer trapped tube (apparent horizon), emerging and smooth (except at a point) and spacelike.
status_evidence.claim: Conditional results on extension of trapped surfaces to spacelike tubes exist; general persistence is not established.
